text.p: Italian bond futures started lower reflecting other easier European bond markets with German bunds showing technical weakness and French bonds sharply off on fears of a call for snap elections, dealers said.

They added that there were also reports over the weekend of an IMF report critical of Italy's 1997 mini-budget because it did not address structural problems. Lira and dollar also weak and contributing to early BTP weakness.
Focus of market likely to be on first six Italian cities reporting preliminary April CPI later today when the CPI is seen dipping under two percent and may prompt an interest rate cut.
Dealers point out that French bonds and the franc were weak as the market waited to see whether President Chirac will call snap French parliamentary elections this morning.
"We are looking abroad for initial direction, but there is again doubts over Italy's entry into EMU in the background worrying the market," said one trader on the LIFFE market.

Analysts expect that the first six Italian cities report on preliminary April CPI later today will show CPI dipping to 1.8 percent from 2.2 percent in March. Milan, Turin, Venice, Trieste, Naples and Bari report today with a further five Italian cities on Tuesday.

"This could be the last chance the Bank of Italy gets to cut rates, so we would expect some move in the discount rate before the end of the month, and possibly soon after the figures," said the LIFFE trader.
